case_name: Dilbag Singh And Another vs State Of Punjab And Another

parties.respondent_defendant: State of Punjab and another (government agency)

facts_of_case: Petitioner's daughter was married to Dilbag Singh. In-laws started torturing her. Petitioners seek quashing of FIR and all subsequent proceedings.

legal_principles.principle: A compromise deed is binding on the parties and must be honoured.
legal_principles.held: It has been held in paras 5 to 8 by the Apex Court that a compromise deed is binding on the parties and must be honoured.
cited_cases: Ruchi Agarwal vs. Amit Kumar Agarwal, (2005) 3 SCC 299

legal_principles.principle: A party who has obtained a divorce under Section 13-B of the Hindu Marriage Act must honour the terms of the compromise deed.
legal_principles.held: It is based on the said compromise that the appellant obtained a divorce as desired by her under Section 13(B) of the Hindu Marriage Act and in partial compliance of the terms of the compromise she withdrew the criminal case filed under Section 125 of the Criminal Procedure Code.
cited_cases: Ruchi Agarwal vs. Amit Kumar Agarwal, (2005) 3 SCC 299

outcome.final_order: FIR No. 179 dated 19.9.2006 under Sections 406,498-A IPC registered at Police Station City Kapurthala is quashed.

use_for_drafting: petition under Section 482 Cr.P.C. for family court
